agree.reason: The GM thinks the renovation drove the scores, and the memo's modest 'helped' claim and its budget plan will make him take the case seriously, but it never says why six years here plus seven weeks running the department beat an outsider's experience at a bigger front desk, so he may stay undecided.

honest.reason: It doesn't make the 'main reason' claim the writer wanted, gives the renovation its due, and invents no numbers; the claims that turnover cut recruiting spend and supervisor time are reasonable inferences but aren't supported by any figures.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that training is about 45% faster and that turnover fell from about 64% to about 36%, both correct and favourably framed, but it misses easy figures like four fewer departures a year or the 0.7-point score gain.

right_comparison.reason: It compares turnover and training before and after the writer took over, but never sets the writer against the real alternative, an outside hire who would need time to learn this hotel and its team.

qualification.reason: The budget hedge comes with a checkable deliverable (a payroll forecast and labor plan by day 90), but it gives no measure of success and no consequence if the plan isn't met.

objections.reason: It answers the renovation objection head-on by arguing the check-in score measures the desk experience, and it answers the budget gap, but it never takes on the outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel.

fit.reason: It's a one-page written memo, as asked, with clear headed sections and placeholders the writer can fill in.
